title: RAG, Vectors & Graphs
subtitle: How systems find evidence, connect facts, and ground answers
footer: Recorded-class synthesis + expanded notes • class numbers omitted

bands.heading: RAG means relevance-selected evidence
bands.deck: A generation architecture, not a synonym for every external tool call

nodes.label: User question
nodes.note: Ask for an explanation, policy, procedure, or other knowledge

nodes.label: Candidate space
nodes.note: There may be thousands of documents, chunks, nodes, or passages

nodes.label: Relevance step
nodes.note: Rank, filter, or traverse to choose evidence for this query

nodes.label: Context assembly
nodes.note: Place selected evidence beside the question and instructions

nodes.label: Grounded answer
nodes.note: Generate from that bundle, cite it, or say evidence is missing

bands.heading: RAG versus a generic tool call
bands.deck: The same call-and-return mechanics can serve different architectural roles

nodes.label: RAG retrieval
items: Select by similarity, ranking, or traversal

nodes.label: Known lookup
items: The key or record is already known
Fetch one current value or state
Return the value to the model

nodes.label: Action tool
items: Not RAG just because text returns

bands.heading: Three questions that look alike
bands.deck: The user's wording does not tell you the architecture; the retrieval role does

bands.heading: Two pipelines, one handoff
bands.deck: Offline preparation shapes what the online answer can recover

nodes.label: Load sources
nodes.note: Bring in PDFs, notes, pages, tables, or other approved material

nodes.label: Split ideas
nodes.note: Create focused chunks without cutting the meaning in half

nodes.label: Embed + store
nodes.note: Save vectors beside chunk text, source identity, and metadata

nodes.label: Embed the question
nodes.note: Represent the live query in the same semantic space

nodes.label: Retrieve + generate
nodes.note: Select evidence, assemble context, and produce a grounded answer

bands.heading: A vector is a point in meaning space
bands.deck: Text becomes geometry so related ideas can be found without matching words

nodes.label: Text
nodes.note: A sentence, paragraph, or question

nodes.label: Chunk
nodes.note: The smallest useful unit we want to recover

nodes.label: Embedding
nodes.note: A numeric position that represents the chunk's meaning

nodes.label: Similarity
nodes.note: Compare directions and distance in semantic space

nodes.label: Top K
nodes.note: Keep the few candidates that best fit the query

bands.heading: Chunking controls signal quality
bands.deck: The chunk is the unit of retrieval, context, cost, and possible confusion

bands.heading: Retrieval has several quality dials
bands.deck: A good answer depends on both the search space and the amount of evidence returned

nodes.label: Embed query
nodes.note: Turn the question into the same kind of vector as stored chunks

nodes.label: Filter metadata
nodes.note: Limit by source, type, date, tenant, or other trusted attributes

nodes.label: Compare candidates
nodes.note: Use cosine similarity, lexical ranking, graph paths, or a mix

nodes.label: Choose Top K
nodes.note: Too few misses context; too many dilute attention with noise

nodes.label: Rerank + inspect
nodes.note: Reorder candidates, reject weak evidence, and check the fit

bands.heading: Where vector search lives
bands.deck: The same database can support RAG or lookup depending on the query's purpose

nodes.label: Postgres + pgvector
items: Useful when relational data already dominates

nodes.label: Qdrant
items: Good fit for chunk retrieval at scale

bands.heading: Graph databases model connections directly
bands.deck: The answer may depend on a path through entities, not on the nearest paragraph

nodes.label: Entity
nodes.note: Represent a person, product, table, pipeline, incident, or team

nodes.label: Relationship
nodes.note: Store an explicit link with direction, type, and meaning

nodes.label: Properties
nodes.note: Keep useful facts on nodes and relationships, not only in prose

nodes.label: Traverse
nodes.note: Follow several links to answer a connected question

nodes.label: Impact path
nodes.note: Explain lineage, dependencies, and the radius of a failure

bands.heading: One question can fan out across evidence types
bands.deck: A retriever can use several paths, then return one curated context

nodes.label: Question
nodes.note: Start with the user's information need and constraints

nodes.label: Retriever hub
nodes.note: Decide which evidence paths can answer this kind of question

nodes.label: Search paths
nodes.note: Use semantic vectors, graph traversal, keyword ranking, or a hybrid

nodes.label: Curated bundle
nodes.note: Keep the strongest passages, nodes, links, and supporting metadata

nodes.label: Context window
nodes.note: Fit the evidence inside a bounded prompt with clear instructions

nodes.label: Grounded answer
nodes.note: Generate from the bundle and preserve the trail back to sources

bands.heading: Vector, graph, keyword, hybrid
bands.deck: Each mechanism answers a different relevance question

nodes.label: Graph search
items: Useful when relationships carry the answer

bands.heading: From raw hits to usable context
bands.deck: Retrieval is not finished when results arrive; context still needs editorial work

nodes.label: Candidate results
nodes.note: Collect passages, nodes, edges, scores, and source metadata

nodes.label: Deduplicate
nodes.note: Remove repeated or overlapping evidence before it crowds the prompt

nodes.label: Rerank
nodes.note: Prefer evidence that is both relevant and useful for this question

nodes.label: Budget context
nodes.note: Fit enough coverage without burying the signal in a giant window

nodes.label: Add guardrails
nodes.note: Require source-aware answers, clear delimiters, and an honest fallback

bands.heading: The litmus test: retrieve or look up?
bands.deck: Ask whether the system chooses relevant evidence or fetches known state

nodes.label: Is there a large knowledge space?
nodes.note: Many candidate documents, chunks, nodes, or passages could answer

nodes.label: Does the step select relevance?
nodes.note: Similarity, traversal, filtering, lexical ranking, or reranking

nodes.label: Does the result ground generation?
nodes.note: The model should use external evidence rather than rely on memory

nodes.label: Is the source trail useful?
nodes.note: A good RAG result lets a reader inspect where the claim came from

nodes.label: Or is it known state?
nodes.note: Fetch a row, check a balance, read a price, or call an action

nodes.label: If unsure, name the role
nodes.note: The mechanism can look identical; the architectural purpose decides

bands.heading: Choose memory by question shape
bands.deck: Use the simplest retrieval strategy that answers the question well

nodes.label: What kind of request is this?

children.label: Document or explanation → vector or keyword retrieval
Known current value or side effect → direct lookup or tool

bands.heading: Keep the answer honest
bands.deck: The database is not the answer; evidence quality is the guardrail

nodes.label: Can the source be named?
nodes.note: Show the document, node, path, or record behind the claim

nodes.label: Does the evidence fit?
nodes.note: Reject irrelevant chunks, broken links, and convenient but weak matches

nodes.label: Is the question fresh?
nodes.note: Refresh mutable state instead of pretending a static corpus is current

nodes.label: What if nothing matches?
nodes.note: Say what is unknown rather than filling the gap from model memory

nodes.label: Is this an action boundary?
nodes.note: Keep side effects and permissions explicit; do not disguise them as retrieval

nodes.label: Can we measure it?
nodes.note: Track recall, precision, latency, cost, citations, and failure cases
